real_project_verdict_notes: LLC chain, IA (executed 2022-09-12), Ch.313 agreement, and TX SOS filings all confirm a real, active developer. The interconnection facilities (Tiger Creek Switch + companion Jaguar BESS) are BUILT and imagery-confirmed complete since mid-2025, with EIA-860M reporting the BESS '(OP) Operating'. But the 300 MW AC solar array itself has not visibly broken ground as of the 2026-07-21 imagery refresh -- hence 'early' rather than 'active': real project, infrastructure-first build sequence, solar PV construction still pending.

site.method: EIA-860M generator pin for 'PP Jaguar BESS LLC' (co-located BESS sharing the same Point of Interconnection / switchyard as Jaguar Solar — IA Exhibit C names both 24INR0038 and BESS 24INR0039 at one 'Tiger Creek Switch' collector station), cross-validated by independently georeferencing the Ch.313 App #1688 Tab-11a 'Project Boundary and Project Vicinity Map' (sources/..._app_p31.png county-wide, p32.png zoomed) — 5-point affine fit on OSM-geocoded place labels visible on the map (Ross, Tours, Leroy, Axtell, Mt Calm; all residuals <70m) puts the red project-boundary centroid at 31.602,-96.975, ~470m from the EIA pin. Sentinel-2 imagery (2026-07-21 refresh) confirms a real substation/BESS complex sits exactly at the EIA coordinate: absent/bare-graded in the earliest available chip (2024-07-19) and complete by 2025-07-17, matching the reported BESS Phase I mechanical completion (2025-04-02). Upgraded from the prior 'medium' confidence Tradinghouse-substation proxy, which was only the transmission line's south terminus, not the project site.

sam_switch.notes: Sam Switch is in Hill County, NOT McLennan County. It is a 345kV switching station off Hill County Road 3165. No OSM/Nominatim result found — no confirmed coordinates.
sam_switch.source: Web search results citing county road reference

infrastructure.tap_notes: The 345kV transmission line runs from Tradinghouse SES (McLennan County) north/northwest to Sam Switch (Hill County). The ERCOT EIR 'Venus Switch to Sam Switch' PDF (Dec 2024) covers a related 38-mile Oncor line in the same corridor.

tiger_creek_switch.quote: The Point of Interconnection is located in McLennan County, Texas, at TSP's Tiger Creek Switch in TSP's Sam Switch - Tradinghouse SES 345 kV transmission line.
tiger_creek_switch.note: NEW substation built by Oncor specifically for this interconnection (a loop-in/tap point on the existing Sam Switch-Tradinghouse line, per Exhibit C section 8-9 'Sam Switch (LST) - Tradinghouse Switch 345 kV Transmission Line Modifications' and 'Tiger Creek Switch - Generator 345 kV Transmission Line Addition'), NOT the same location as Tradinghouse SES or Sam Switch themselves. Its precise stated distance/bearing in Exhibit C and the Attachment 4 vicinity map are both REDACTED in the filed copy. Site coordinate above (31.59992,-96.97054) is the imagery-verified location of the built Tiger Creek Switch + Jaguar BESS complex.

construction.assessment: Imagery-verified 2026-07-21 at 31.59992,-96.97054 (buffer 3.5km, 5 dates 2024-07 -> 2026-07): a compact bright-white switchyard/BESS-building complex (Tiger Creek Switch + Jaguar BESS) is visible at the exact EIA-pin location, unchanged in footprint from 2025-07-17 through 2026-07-19 -- matches the reported BESS Phase I mechanical completion (2025-04-02) and its EIA-860M '(OP) Operating' status (as of 2025-12). The 2024-07-19 frame shows the same footprint as bare graded earth, confirming this is the construction site (not a pre-existing structure). NO utility-scale solar PV array (large dark/textured panel-row block) is visible anywhere in the full 7km x 7km survey area at any of the 5 dates, including the most recent pass (2026-07-19) -- the 300 MW AC solar field itself has NOT visibly broken ground as of this refresh, consistent with the queue's repeated COD slips (now 2027-12-11) and McLennan County's Mar-2026 Road Use Agreement (site-access negotiation, not yet active construction). A brief striped/ribbed sun-glint pattern on the switchyard gantry structures in the 2026-04-15 frame was initially mistaken for panel racking on close inspection but is the same fixed substation footprint seen in every other frame -- not a separate PV installation. Neighbor check against data/eia_generator_tx.parquet (McLennan County, latest reportDate 2026-05-01): no other named plant (Copperhead Solar, Sandy Creek Energy Station, Pepper Solar Farm, Griffin Solar, etc.) falls within the 3.5km imagery buffer, so no attribution risk from this frame; Tokio Solar (23INR0349, sibling project/directory) is ~30km away, unrelated.
